gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Galaxy Tab S11's included S Pen has no Bluetooth: Samsung lists no Air Actions on the Tab S11 even with the $99-class S Pen Pro, its tip doesn't fit earlier S Pens, and the $144.99 Book Cover Keyboard Slim has no trackpad or pen holder according to owner reviews on Samsung's US page; ChatGPT's alternative, the Lenovo Yoga Tab, has no microSD slot at all.
standout_why: Compared against the three pages ChatGPT cited plus Android Authority (top result #14). iTechGuides (cited) says only that the redesigned S Pen is 'exclusive to the S11 series' and that the A11+ is 'Not compatible'. Tech Advisor (cited) says only 'Excellent bundled S Pen stylus' and 'No charger'. Android Authority says 'Redesigned S Pen' and 'No S Pen support' for the A11+. None of them mention the missing Bluetooth or Air Actions, that the tip won't fit older S Pens, the keyboard's limits, or the Yoga Tab's missing card reader. I could not read Wired's pages (fetch blocked), and the Tom's Guide, Android Central and TechRadar pages came back truncated, so I can't rule those out.
decides: It confirms the Tab S11 for drawing and notes, but with a stated limit: the pen is a passive, battery-free stylus with no remote camera shutter or gesture control, and buying an S Pen Pro doesn't bring Air Actions back on this tablet. A shopper who used Air Actions on a Tab S9 should know that before upgrading. It also cuts against ChatGPT's 'best value' Lenovo Yoga Tab for anyone who needs expandable storage, because the Yoga Tab has no card reader while every Samsung pick takes microSD up to 2 TB. The Tab A11+ stays a no-pen option.

Samsung US-page wattage for Tab S11 charging: the US product page says only 'Super Fast Charging'; 45 W comes from Samsung's Uzbekistan support page.

US price and part number of the Lenovo Keyboard Pack for Yoga Tab sold separately: PSREF lists it only as a bundled accessory.
